report:
**Conclusion: the claim is not supported.** There is no reliable clinical evidence that drinking boiled garlic water cures COVID-19. WHO’s myth-busting guidance specifically says garlic has some antimicrobial properties but there is **no evidence** it prevents COVID-19; that falls far short of evidence for a cure. https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/advice-for-public/myth-busters

The closest relevant human research is not a test of garlic water: a small phase-II trial examined **TD0068**, a standardized multi-ingredient traditional medicine containing garlic extract, in adults with *non-severe* COVID-19. That cannot establish that boiled garlic water works, nor that it cures infection. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37637574/

For people at higher risk of severe disease, CDC recommends prompt evaluation for authorized antiviral treatment rather than substituting home remedies; benefits depend on starting treatment early. https://www.cdc.gov/covid/hcp/clinical-care/outpatient-treatment.html

Garlic used as food is generally different from concentrated supplements, but it is not risk-free: oral garlic can cause stomach symptoms or allergy, and supplements can increase bleeding risk—important for people using anticoagulants or before surgery. https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/garlic

If you have COVID-19 symptoms or a positive test, use testing/isolation guidance and contact a clinician promptly—especially if you are older, pregnant, immunocompromised, or have chronic conditions. Do not delay proven care for garlic water.
